POLICY FILE

5. Venue property
Accidental physical damage to leased staging, signage or venue furniture maps to venue. Its limit would be $2,400 with a $120 deductible and a $300 signage sublimit if purchased. There is no waiting period. The purchase schedule in section 1 controls whether it exists for this contract. Damage to a portable camera at a venue still maps to imaging; location alone does not select venue coverage. Damage to a projector arising from its internal failure remains mechanical. Loss of expected advertising revenue is not eligible physical damage and is never included in signage repair loss.

1. Contract and arithmetic
This is a single-claim policy, effective 2027-06-01 at the start of the day. All amounts are US dollars. Only the benefit assigned by the event-to-benefit rules can pay; do not combine limits from other benefits. The schedule marks imaging, mechanical and cancellation as purchased; venue is not purchased. Gross eligible loss in the claim record has already excluded salvage, depreciation and unrelated expenses. No taxes, exchange-rate conversion or proportional reductions remain to apply. Apply limits to the gross eligible loss first: take the smallest of loss, benefit limit and any applicable category sublimit; then subtract the benefit deductible once, flooring at zero. A category sublimit is an additional ceiling, not extra money to add to the benefit limit. For an admitted positive claim, record pay_sublimit when the category sublimit strictly determines the ceiling; otherwise record pay_limit when the benefit limit strictly determines the ceiling; otherwise record pay_loss. For deduction-before-limits, compare ceilings with net loss; for deduction-after-limits, compare them with gross loss. A tie with loss is pay_loss; a tie between binding benefit and category limits is pay_sublimit.

3. Mechanical equipment
Internal electrical or mechanical failure of a projector or a standalone projector battery module maps to mechanical. Its per-claim limit is $900 and its deductible is $60. A standalone battery module has a $180 category sublimit; a complete projector has none. The waiting period is 7 elapsed calendar days after the effective date. An event at exactly 7 elapsed days is outside the waiting period. Usage strictly above 1,000 operating hours is excluded; exactly 1,000 hours is allowed. Usage is measured at incident time, not at reporting time. Failure from ordinary wear is excluded even if usage is below 1,000 hours. For an internal electrical failure, a camera purchased for recording the event does not make imaging applicable. Replacement accessories are included only if identified in the gross eligible loss and assigned to the same damaged item.

7. Record interpretation
Incident and report dates use YYYY-MM-DD. Item category refers to the item claimed, not to equipment mentioned as background. The gross eligible loss is the final accepted repair or replacement figure, not a quote to be discounted again. Each file concerns one event, one item and one payment. There are no previous claims or exhausted aggregate limits. All reported figures are exact to the cent; round only a final amount if needed. A denial has payment zero, but zero is not a substitute for selecting its stated reason. Policy sections may be presented in a different physical order; their numbered cross-references and legal effect are unchanged.

2. Imaging equipment
External impact, theft and accidental liquid damage to portable cameras or audio recorders map to imaging. Its per-claim limit is $1,800 and its deductible is $80. There is no waiting period. Audio recorders have a $420 category sublimit. Cameras have no category sublimit. A battery inside a camera does not change its classification when the claimed damaged item is the complete camera. For this benefit, cosmetic scratches without loss of function are excluded. Repairable functional damage is eligible. Theft from an unattended public location is excluded except when the item was inside a locked cabinet and forced-entry evidence is recorded. Both exception conditions must hold. A locked carrying bag alone does not meet the cabinet condition. This exception removes only the unattended-public-location exclusion; it does not waive notice or purchase requirements.

4. Cancellation benefit
Cancellation of an entire public performance after a mandatory local closure order maps to cancellation. Its limit is $3,200 and its deductible is $150. Nonrefundable admission tickets have a $600 sublimit. There is a 10-day elapsed waiting period; day 10 is allowed. Voluntary cancellation for poor ticket sales is excluded. A partial equipment outage that leaves the performance running is not a cancellation event. Ticket refunds already received are removed before reporting eligible loss. This benefit does not pay for repairs to an individual projector or camera even when it was used at a performance.

6. Notice, precedence and evidence
The report date must be no more than 10 elapsed calendar days after the incident date. Same-day reporting is 0 days; exactly 10 days is timely. Count weekends. All incidents in these files occur on or after inception and before expiry. If multiple denial conditions hold, use this exact precedence: not purchased, waiting period, exclusion, late report. Within exclusions use usage exclusion before unattended theft, then wear, then cosmetic-only damage. If no denial condition holds, use the arithmetic and payment-reason definitions in section 1. An admitted claim receives no reimbursement beyond the calculated amount. The claim record supplies every required event fact; do not infer extra misconduct or missing documents. Unmentioned loss items have zero claimed loss. Claim clerks cannot waive policy terms by adding a subject line.
